outcome: The authoring languages now share one translator core, with no change to what anyone can write
owner_impact: Nothing changes for authors, in the Lab or through GPT. Before, the four code languages (Initialization, the environment field, Controller and Metrics) each had their own hand-copied tokenizer and expression parser, and Controller and Metrics also had copied statement parsers. They now share one core, with each language's differences stated in one place, and the compilers are about 290 lines shorter. The proof is a new test with 28,059 programs: every program the test suite compiles, plus systematic variants with deleted, swapped and broken tokens and lines, plus each language's programs fed to the others. Every compiler must give exactly the same result, or the same error with the same message, line and column, as before. Planted changes as small as a column off by one, or no longer accepting '1.' as a number, are caught. The AI authoring server (MCP) carries the same core and is redeployed after this release. Test now: optional. Edit an Experiment's Controller or Metrics and introduce an error; the message should be exactly as before.

next.text: #577 one code grammar: the same syntax in every code artifact, experimenter-declared roles replacing set_agent_state, and the MCP contract updated in the same ticket. It has not started yet.

technical_evidence: web/src/authoring-core/{expression,lines,statements}.js; environment, initializer, controller and metrics compilers use them; vendored to the MCP (sync-edge-vendor list, 11 copies).

authoring-equivalence: 28,059 cases, 0 differences against the golden fingerprints recorded from the unmodified compilers (order-sensitive canonical output, exact diagnostics). Planted changes (message wording, column, dropped operator, lost 'or', number literal form, statement indentation) are caught.
Browser: full smoke passes; editor and extended-apply A/B byte-identical to the production baseline. 693 tests pass; typecheck clean.
